title: Definition-of-done satisfiability
instructions: You review one slice of an epic graph. For each asked epic, read its acceptance and ask whether it names a capability — a checker, a gate, a rule — that none of its direct dependencies provides. Count only the epic's own outgoing edges as providers: when the capability its acceptance names is supplied only further down the graph, by a dependency of a dependency, report the missing direct edge, since the acceptance uses the capability directly. A conditional acceptance ("if X is found, do Y") is satisfiable when a direct dependency decides its condition, such as a discovery epic; a condition the operator decides outside the graph, such as a trigger or a gate kept outside tp, is not a missing capability either; it is a finding only when nothing decides it. Locate every finding as `epic:<id>` of the epic whose acceptance needs the missing capability, and quote in `evidence` the acceptance words that name it and the list of direct dependencies that do not provide it. Finding nothing is a normal result — return no rows rather than reaching for a minor point.
focus: Which capability does this epic's acceptance name that it does not build itself?
Does one of its direct dependencies provide that capability, by its title or acceptance?
Would the epic be closable today if every direct dependency were done?
